court: Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction under Tucker Act
issues.why: The court must confirm it has subject-matter jurisdiction over each money-mandating claim against the United States.

issues.label: Proper defendant is United States
issues.why: The court must ensure claims are asserted against the United States rather than an agency or officials.

issues.label: Administrative record scope
issues.why: The court must decide what constitutes the full administrative record for reviewing the Board’s decision.

issues.label: Standard of review applied
issues.why: The court must apply the correct APA-like standard (arbitrary/capricious/substantial evidence/contrary to law) to BCMR/BCNR decisions.

issues.label: Deference to military judgments
issues.why: The court must account for heightened deference in military fitness and personnel determinations while still enforcing legal limits.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must identify who bears the burden to show error/injustice and what evidentiary standard applies (preponderance/substantial evidence).

issues.label: Exhaustion of remedies
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mr. Qoye exhausted required administrative remedies before suing.

issues.label: Final agency action
issues.why: The court must confirm the challenged Board decision is final and reviewable.

issues.label: Statute of limitations accrual
issues.why: The court must determine when each claim accrued for 28 U.S.C. § 2501 purposes.

issues.label: Separate accrual per claim
issues.why: The court must separately analyze accrual for disability retirement pay, bonus recoupment/refund, and record-correction relief.

issues.label: Disability retirement claim accrual
issues.why: The court must decide when the disability-retirement claim became fixed (e.g., at discharge vs. Board denial).

issues.label: Bonus refund claim accrual
issues.why: The court must decide when the bonus recoupment/refund claim accrued (recoupment decision/payment vs. discharge).

issues.label: Record-correction claim accrual
issues.why: The court must decide when the correction-of-record claim accrued (when record created vs. Board denial).

issues.label: Equitable tolling availability
issues.why: The court must determine whether § 2501 permits tolling and whether any asserted grounds could apply.

issues.label: Continuing claim doctrine
issues.why: The court must assess whether periodic retired pay creates a continuing claim or whether the initial entitlement decision controls accrual.

issues.label: Claim preclusion issues
issues.why: The court must consider whether prior administrative or judicial determinations bar any issues now raised.

issues.label: Issue preservation/waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether arguments not presented to the Board are waived or can be considered.

issues.label: Remand order compliance
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the Board on remand addressed all issues and relief claims as directed.

issues.label: Adequate explanation requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board provided a rational connection between facts found and conclusions reached.

issues.label: Consideration of relevant factors
issues.why: The court must verify the Board considered all important evidence and factors bearing on fitness, diagnosis, and alleged error/injustice.

issues.label: Ignoring contrary evidence
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board improperly discounted favorable evidence such as lay statements and VA medical opinions.

issues.label: Reliance on wrong records
issues.why: The court must evaluate the legal significance of the informal PEB’s initial reliance on another service member’s records and whether prejudice resulted.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: The court must decide whether any procedural/record errors were harmless or require remand.

issues.label: Fitness-for-duty legal standard
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct statutory/regulatory definition of unfitness (interference with duties at separation) was applied.

issues.label: Time-of-separation focus
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board properly focused on Mr. Qoye’s condition and performance at separation rather than later deterioration.

issues.label: Duty performance evidence weight
issues.why: The court must decide how to weigh performance evaluations against reports of falling asleep and watchstanding problems.

issues.label: Lay evidence credibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how the Board should credit shipmate/supervisor observations of daytime sleep episodes.

issues.label: Medical evidence adequacy
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether in-service medical workup was adequate and what inference follows from missing narcolepsy testing.

issues.label: Failure to refer to MEB/PEB
issues.why: The court must determine whether failure to refer during service was legal error and whether it necessitates disability retirement relief.

issues.label: Causation vs. unfitness distinction
issues.why: The court must separate service connection/causation from the distinct requirement of unfitness for duty for retirement.

issues.label: VA rating relevance
issues.why: The court must decide the probative value of the VA’s 40% service-connected narcolepsy rating in the military fitness context.

issues.label: VA effective date significance
issues.why: The court must assess what inference, if any, follows from VA’s rating effective the day after discharge.

issues.label: Post-service medical opinions weight
issues.why: The court must decide how much weight to give VA physician statements that narcolepsy developed or worsened on active duty.

issues.label: 2010 sleep study interpretation
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board reasonably relied on the 2010 study and its limitations (no narcolepsy testing).

issues.label: Later MSLT test impact
issues.why: The court must decide how the 2012 MSLT narcolepsy-consistent result bears on condition severity at separation.

issues.label: Condition severity at separation
issues.why: The court must determine whether narcolepsy symptoms were severe enough in 2011 to make him incapable of performing required duties.

issues.label: Nuclear duty standards
issues.why: The court must consider heightened reliability/safety standards for nuclear machinist mate duties in evaluating fitness.

issues.label: NEC status factual dispute
issues.why: The court must resolve whether NEC removal actually occurred and what the official record shows.

issues.label: Basis for NEC removal
issues.why: The court must decide whether NEC removal was properly based on misconduct/unreliability or should be tied to medical unfitness.

issues.label: Medical disqualification from NEC
issues.why: The court must determine whether records should reflect a retroactive medical disqualification from the NEC and what standard governs.

issues.label: NJP validity collateral attack
issues.why: The court must decide whether Mr. Qoye can collaterally challenge the NJP basis used to justify NEC removal.

issues.label: NJP-medical mitigation nexus
issues.why: The court must assess whether narcolepsy could mitigate or explain the misconduct leading to NJP and NEC removal.

issues.label: Liberal consideration applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether liberal consideration standards apply to this case despite an honorable discharge.

issues.label: Scope of liberal consideration
issues.why: The court must define what issues liberal consideration could affect (misconduct characterization, medical nexus, or fitness determination).

issues.label: Board’s liberal consideration rationale
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the Board’s stated reason for denying liberal consideration (honorable discharge) was legally correct.

issues.label: Record correction authority limits
issues.why: The court must confirm what corrections the Board/court can order (status, narrative reasons, NEC, retirement category).

issues.label: Entitlement to PDRL placement
issues.why: The court must determine whether, if unfit, the proper remedy is PDRL versus other disability dispositions.

issues.label: Disability rating determination
issues.why: The court must decide what rating would apply for narcolepsy for military disability purposes and whether a rating dispute is before it.

issues.label: Retroactive retired pay calculation
issues.why: The court must determine how to compute any back pay, offsets, and effective dates if retirement is granted.

issues.label: Offsets and recoupments
issues.why: The court must consider statutory offsets (VA compensation, prior separation pay/bonus recoupment) against any retired pay award.

issues.label: Reenlistment bonus recoupment legality
issues.why: The court must interpret the reenlistment contract and governing regulations authorizing recoupment for early separation or NEC loss.

issues.label: Trigger for recoupment met
issues.why: The court must decide whether Mr. Qoye was “no longer classified” in the NEC/rating or failed to complete obligated service, triggering recoupment.

issues.label: Effect of medical retirement on bonus
issues.why: The court must decide whether a medical disability retirement would bar or reverse recoupment and require refund.

issues.label: Reduction-in-force discharge impact
issues.why: The court must determine how the “reduction in force” narrative reason affects entitlement, recoupment, and credibility of the separation basis.

issues.label: Voluntary early separation impact
issues.why: The court must assess whether requesting early separation affects eligibility for disability processing or monetary relief.

issues.label: Causation of separation decision
issues.why: The court must determine whether separation was due to medical condition, misconduct consequences, force reduction, or voluntary request.

issues.label: Rationality of Board factfinding
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board’s fact determinations (fitness, NEC basis) are supported by substantial evidence.

issues.label: Consideration of 2015 job application
issues.why: The court must assess whether reliance on a 2015 military mechanic application reasonably supports a 2011 fitness finding.

issues.label: Substantial evidence definition
issues.why: The court must apply the correct legal definition of substantial evidence in reviewing administrative findings.

issues.label: Arbitrary-and-capricious review
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board’s decision-making process was reasoned, consistent, and non-arbitrary.

issues.label: Contrary to law review
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board misapplied statutes, regulations, or required procedures for disability evaluation.

issues.label: Remedy: remand vs. judgment
issues.why: The court must decide whether any error warrants remand to the Board for further explanation or whether relief can be ordered directly.

issues.label: Scope of permissible relief
issues.why: The court must determine whether requested non-monetary corrections are ancillary to a money claim and within the court’s power.

issues.label: Interest and attorneys’ fees
issues.why: The court must consider whether any statute authorizes interest or fee shifting if Mr. Qoye prevails.

issues.label: Administrative delay relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether long delays in Board/PEB processing affect timeliness, prejudice, or equitable considerations.

issues.label: Record completeness and supplementation
issues.why: The court must decide whether extra-record evidence is admissible to show bad faith, missing documents, or to interpret the record.
